### 2020

::: {.question-card #matrices-2020-mj-11-12}
### 2020 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 6 · 13 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** The transformation represented by $A^{-1}$ maps a triangle of area $30\text{ cm}^2$ to a triangle of area $d\text{ cm}^2$. Find $d$. **[3]**

**(b)** Prove by induction that, for every positive integer $n$,

$$
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**[5]**

Let $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\33&0\end{pmatrix}$.

**(c)** The line $y=2x$ is invariant under the transformation represented by $A^nB$. Find $n$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Since $\det A=2$, $|\det A^{-1}|=\frac12$, so $\boxed{d=15}$.

The formula is true for $n=1$. If it holds for $n=k$, then

$$
A^{k+1}=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2^{k+1}&0\\2^{k+1}-1&1\end{pmatrix},
$$

which completes the induction. Finally,

$$
A^nB=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n+32&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$

For its image to have gradient $2$, $(2^n+32)/2^n=2$, giving $2^n=32$ and $\boxed{n=5}$.

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2020-mj-11-12"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2020, Q6; 9231/12/M/J/2020, Q6.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #matrices-2020-mj-13}
### 2020 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 4 · 11 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}k&0&2\\0&-1&-1\\1&1&-k\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&-3\\-1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}-3&-1&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Show that $A$ is non-singular. **[3]**

It is given that

$$
CAB=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-\frac32\\-1&-\frac32\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(b)** Find $k$. **[3]**

**(c)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $CAB$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Expanding $\det A$ gives $k^2+k+2$, whose discriminant is $1-8<0$; hence it is never zero for real $k$.

Multiplying $CAB$ and comparing entries gives $\boxed{k=-\frac12}$. For $y=mx$, the condition $Y=mX$ gives

$$
-1-\frac32m=m\left(-2-\frac32m\right),
$$

so $3m^2+m-2=0$. Therefore

$$
\boxed{y=\frac23x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2020-mj-13"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2020, Q4.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #matrices-2020-on-11-13}
### 2020 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 1 · 9 marks

Let

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $a,b>0$.

**(a)** State the two transformations represented by $M$, in the correct order. **[2]**

The unit square is mapped by $M$ onto parallelogram $OPQR$.

**(b)** Find the matrix mapping $OPQR$ back onto the unit square. **[2]**

**(c)** Given that the area of $OPQR$ is $2\text{ cm}^2$ and $x+3y=0$ is invariant, find $a$ and $b$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

First apply a one-way stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $a$, then a shear with the $x$-axis fixed and shear factor $b$.

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac1a\begin{pmatrix}1&-b\\0&a\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

The area factor is $|\det M|=a$, so $a=2$. A point $(x,-x/3)$ on the invariant line maps to $(ax-bx/3,-x/3)$. Requiring it to remain on the same line gives $1=a-b/3$, hence $\boxed{a=2, b=3}$.

</details>

<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2020, Q1; 9231/13/O/N/2020, Q1.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #matrices-2020-on-12}
### 2020 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 13 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Identify the transformation represented by $A$. **[1]**

**(b)** Identify the transformation represented by $B$. **[2]**

Triangle $DEF$ is transformed by $AB$ onto triangle $PQR$.

**(c)** Show that the two triangles have the same area. **[3]**

**(d)** Find the matrix mapping $PQR$ onto $DEF$. **[2]**

**(e)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $AB$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$A$ is reflection in $y=x$; $B$ is rotation through $60^\circ$ anticlockwise about the origin. Also

$$
AB=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\\[2pt]\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det(AB)=-1,
$$

so the absolute area factor is $1$. Since $AB$ is a reflection, it is self-inverse:

$$
\boxed{(AB)^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\\[2pt]\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

Putting $y=mx$ and using $Y=mX$ gives $m^2+2\sqrt3m-1=0$. Hence

$$
\boxed{y=(2-\sqrt3)x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-(2+\sqrt3)x}.
$$

{{< include figures/matrices/past-2020-on-12.svg >}}

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2020-on-12"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2020, Q4.</div>
:::

### 2021

::: {.question-card #matrices-2021-mj-11-12}
### 2021 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 4 · 14 marks

A rotation of $60^\circ$ anticlockwise about the origin is followed by a one-way stretch in the $x$-direction with scale factor $d$, where $d\ne0$.

**(a)** Find the matrix $M$ of the combined transformation. **[4]**

**(b)** The unit square is mapped by $M$ onto a parallelogram of area $\frac12d^2$. Show that $d=2$. **[2]**

Let $N$ satisfy

$$
MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\[2pt]\frac12&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(c)** Find $N$. **[3]**

**(d)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $MN$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}d&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}\frac d2&-\frac{d\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Since $|\det M|=d$, $d=\frac12d^2$ and $d\ne0$, so $\boxed{d=2}$. Then

$$
\boxed{N=\frac14\begin{pmatrix}1+\sqrt3&1+\sqrt3\\1-\sqrt3&1-\sqrt3\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

For $MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1/2&1/2\end{pmatrix}$, the condition $Y=mX$ gives $2m^2+m-1=0$. Thus

$$
\boxed{y=\frac12x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
$$

</details>

::: {.question-card #matrices-2021-mj-13}
### 2021 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 4 · 11 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&k&k\\5&-1&3\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\-1&2&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Find $CAB$. **[3]**

**(b)** Given that $A$ is singular, find $k$. **[3]**

**(c)** Using this value of $k$, find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $CAB$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$$
CAB=\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}10&-1\\14-k&-k-2\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

Setting $\det A=0$ gives $k=\boxed{-2}$, and hence $CAB=\begin{pmatrix}10&-1\\16&0\end{pmatrix}$. For $y=mx$,

$$
16=m(10-m),
$$

so $m^2-10m+16=0$. Therefore $\boxed{y=2x}$ or $\boxed{y=8x}$.

</details>

### 2021 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 4 · 11 marks

Let

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** State the two transformations represented by $M$, in the correct order. **[2]**

**(b)** For $0\le\theta\le\pi$, find the values of $\theta$ for which the transformation has exactly one invariant line through the origin. **[9]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

First apply a one-way stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $3$, then rotate anticlockwise through $\theta$ about the origin.

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}3\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\3\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.
$$

For $y=mx$, $Y=mX$ reduces to

$$
m^2\sin\theta-2m\cos\theta+3\sin\theta=0.
$$

Exactly one invariant line requires a repeated root, so

$$
4\cos^2\theta-12\sin^2\theta=0.
$$

In the stated interval, $\boxed{\theta=\frac\pi6\text{ or }\frac{5\pi}6}$.

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2021-on-11-13"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2021, Q4; 9231/13/O/N/2021, Q4.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #matrices-2021-on-12}
### 2021 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 1 · 9 marks

**(a)** Describe the transformation represented by $\begin{pmatrix}6&0\\0&6\end{pmatrix}$. **[1]**

Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\2&2\end{pmatrix}$.

**(b)** A triangle of area $13\text{ cm}^2$ is transformed by $A$. Find the area of its image. **[2]**

**(c)** Find $B$ such that $AB=\begin{pmatrix}6&0\\0&6\end{pmatrix}$. **[2]**

**(d)** Show that the origin is the only invariant point of the transformation represented by $A$. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Part (a) is an enlargement, centre the origin, scale factor $6$. Since $\det A=-2$, the image area is $2(13)=\boxed{26\text{ cm}^2}$.

$$
\boxed{B=6A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}-6&12\\6&-9\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

An invariant point $(x,y)$ satisfies $3x+4y=x$ and $2x+2y=y$. These reduce to $2x+4y=0$ and $2x+y=0$, whose only solution is $\boxed{(0,0)}$.

</details>

### 2022

::: {.question-card #matrices-2022-mj-11-12}
### 2022 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 7 · 17 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\4&k&6\\7&8&9\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Find the set of values of $k$ for which $A$ is non-singular. **[3]**

**(b)** Given that $A$ is non-singular, find the entries in the top row of $A^{-1}$. **[4]**

Let $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$.

**(c)** Give an example of a matrix $C$ such that

$$
BAC=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\k&4\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**[4]**

**(d)** Find the set of values of $k$ for which the transformation represented by $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\k&4\end{pmatrix}$ has two distinct invariant lines through the origin. **[6]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$$
\det A=60-12k,
$$

so $\boxed{k\ne5}$. Cofactors give the top row

$$
\boxed{\left(\frac{3k-16}{4(5-k)},\ \frac1{2(5-k)},\ \frac{4-k}{4(5-k)}\right)}.
$$

One valid choice is

$$
\boxed{C=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

For the final matrix, $y=mx$ gives

$$
m^2-2m-k=0.
$$

Two distinct invariant lines require discriminant $4+4k>0$; the represented transformation must also be non-singular, so $8-k\ne0$. Therefore

$$
\boxed{k>-1,\qquad k\ne8}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2022-mj-11-12"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2022, Q7; 9231/12/M/J/2022, Q7.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #matrices-2022-mj-13}
### 2022 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 5 · 12 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $a>0$.

**(a)** State the type of transformation represented by $A$. **[1]**

**(b)** Prove by induction that

$$
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}1&na\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
$$

for every positive integer $n$. **[5]**

Let

$$
B=\begin{pmatrix}b&b\\1/a&1/a\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $b>0$.

**(c)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $A^nB$. **[6]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$A$ represents a shear in the $x$-direction, with the $x$-axis fixed. The formula is true for $n=1$. Assuming it for $n=k$,

$$
A^{k+1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&ka\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&(k+1)a\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
$$

which completes the induction. Also

$$
A^nB=\begin{pmatrix}b+n&b+n\\1/a&1/a\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Using $y=mx$ and $Y=mX$ gives $(1+m)\{1/a-m(b+n)\}=0$. Hence

$$
\boxed{y=-x\quad\text{or}\quad y=\frac{x}{a(b+n)}}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2022-mj-13"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2022, Q5.</div>

### 2023

::: {.question-card #matrices-2023-on-11-13}
### 2023 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 5 · 15 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&k&3\\2&1&3\\3&2&5\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\-1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1&1\\1&1&3\end{pmatrix}.
$$

It is given that $A$ is singular.

**(a)** Show that $CAB=\begin{pmatrix}3&-7\\-9&3\end{pmatrix}$. **[5]**

**(b)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $CAB$. **[5]**

Matrices $D,E,F$ represent, respectively, an enlargement centred at the origin, a stretch parallel to the $x$-axis, and reflection in $y=x$.

**(c)** Given that $CAB=D-9EF$, find $D,E,F$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$\det A=0$ gives $k=2$; direct multiplication then gives the stated $CAB$. For $y=mx$,

$$
-9+3m=m(3-7m),
$$

so $7m^2=9$ and

$$
\boxed{y=\frac3{\sqrt7}x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-\frac3{\sqrt7}x}.
$$

Writing $D=\alpha I$, $E=\begin{pmatrix}\beta&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $F=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and comparing entries gives

$$
\boxed{D=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix},\quad
E=\begin{pmatrix}7/9&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
F=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2023-on-11-13"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2023, Q5; 9231/13/O/N/2023, Q5.</div>

::: {.question-card #matrices-2023-on-12}
### 2023 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 3 · 8 marks

Let

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $k\ne0,1$.

**(a)** State the two transformations represented by $M$, in the correct order. **[2]**

The unit square is transformed by $M$ onto parallelogram $OPQR$.

**(b)** Find its area and the matrix mapping $OPQR$ back onto the unit square. **[3]**

**(c)** Show that the line through the origin with gradient $1/(k-1)$ is invariant. **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

First apply a shear in the $y$-direction with the $y$-axis fixed, then a one-way stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $k$. Since

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix},
$$

the parallelogram has area $\boxed{|k|}$ square units (the official scheme writes $k$, under its geometric scale-factor convention), and

$$
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac1k\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&k\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

For $\mathbf v=\binom{1}{1/(k-1)}$,

$$
M\mathbf v=\binom{k}{k/(k-1)}=k\mathbf v,
$$

which proves invariance.

{{< include figures/matrices/past-2023-on-12.svg >}}

</details>

### 2024

::: {.question-card #matrices-2024-mj-11-12}
### 2024 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 4 · 13 marks

Let

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}14&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Give full details of the two transformations represented by $M$, in the correct order. **[4]**

**(b)** Write $M^{-1}$ as the product of two matrices, neither equal to $I$. **[2]**

**(c)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $M$. **[5]**

Triangle $ABC$ is transformed by $M$ onto triangle $DEF$ of area $28\text{ cm}^2$.

**(d)** Find the area of triangle $ABC$. **[2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

First apply a one-way stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $14$, then rotate anticlockwise through $\pi/3$ about the origin. Reversing the order and inverting each factor gives

$$
\boxed{M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1/14&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

Since

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}7&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]7\sqrt3&\frac12\end{pmatrix},
$$

putting $y=mx$ gives $2\sqrt3m^2-13m+14\sqrt3=0$. Hence

$$
\boxed{y=2\sqrt3x\quad\text{or}\quad y=\frac{7\sqrt3}{3}x}.
$$

Finally $|\det M|=14$, so the original area is $28/14=\boxed{2\text{ cm}^2}$.

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2024-mj-11-12"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Sources:</strong> Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2024, Q4; 9231/12/M/J/2024, Q4.</div>

::: {.question-card #matrices-2024-mj-13-q1}
### 2024 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 1 · 5 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}k&1&0\\6&5&2\\-1&3&-k\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $k$ is real.

**(a)** Show that $A$ is non-singular. **[3]**

**(b)** Given that

$$
A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}3&0&-1\\1&0&0\\-\frac{23}{2}&\frac12&3\end{pmatrix},
$$

find $k$. **[2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Expansion gives

$$
\det A=-5k^2-2,
$$

which is negative for every real $k$ and hence never zero. From $AA^{-1}=I$ (for example, comparing the first entry) one obtains $3k+1=1$, so $\boxed{k=0}$.

</details>

### 2024 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 3 · 11 marks

Let

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}7&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Give full details of the two transformations represented by $M$, in the correct order. **[4]**

**(b)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $M$. **[5]**

Triangle $DEF$ is transformed by $M$ onto triangle $PQR$ of area $35\text{ cm}^2$.

**(c)** Find the area of triangle $DEF$. **[2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

First apply a one-way stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $7$, then a shear with the $x$-axis fixed and $(0,1)$ mapped to $(2,1)$. Thus

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}7&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

For $y=mx$, $Y=mX$ gives $2m^2+6m=0$, so

$$
\boxed{y=0\quad\text{or}\quad y=-3x}.
$$

The area factor is $7$, hence the original area is $35/7=\boxed{5\text{ cm}^2}$.

</details>

<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="matrices-2024-mj-13-q3"> Completed</label>

::: {.question-card #matrices-2024-on-11-13}
### 2024 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 1 · 10 marks

A stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $k\ne0$ is followed by a shear with the $x$-axis fixed and $(0,1)$ mapped to $(k,1)$.

**(a)** Show that the combined matrix is $M=\begin{pmatrix}k&k\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. **[4]**

**(b)** The transformation has a line of invariant points. Find its equation. **[3]**

The unit square $S$ is transformed by $M$ onto parallelogram $P$.

**(c)** Find a matrix mapping $P$ back onto $S$. **[1]**

**(d)** Given that the area of $P$ is $3k^2$, find the possible values of $k$. **[2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

The product in the stated order is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}1&k\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}k&k\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Solving $M\binom xy=\binom xy$ gives

$$
\boxed{y=\frac{1-k}{k}x}.
$$

The reverse matrix is

$$
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac1k\begin{pmatrix}1&-k\\0&k\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

Since the area of $P$ is $|\det M|=|k|$, the condition $|k|=3k^2$ gives $\boxed{k=\pm\frac13}$.

</details>

::: {.question-card #matrices-2024-on-12}
### 2024 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 13 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&1&3\\3&2&5\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\-1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-1&1\\1&1&3\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Show that $CAB=\begin{pmatrix}3&-7\\-9&3\end{pmatrix}$. **[3]**

**(b)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $CAB$. **[5]**

Let $M=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$.

**(c)** Describe the transformation represented by $M$. **[2]**

**(d)** Find $N$ such that $NM=CAB$. **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Direct multiplication gives the stated product. For $y=mx$, the invariance equation gives $7m^2=9$, so

$$
\boxed{y=\frac3{\sqrt7}x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-\frac3{\sqrt7}x}.
$$

$M$ is a one-way stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $3$. Since $N=(CAB)M^{-1}$,

$$
\boxed{N=\begin{pmatrix}1&-7\\-3&3\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

</details>

### 2025

::: {.question-card #matrices-2025-mj-11-12}
### 2025 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 4 · 9 marks

Let

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix},
\qquad 0<\theta<2\pi.
$$

**(a)** State the two transformations represented by $M$, in the correct order. **[2]**

**(b)** Find the value of $\theta$ for which the transformation has a line of invariant points. **[7]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

First rotate anticlockwise through $\theta$ about the origin, then apply a shear with the $x$-axis fixed and $(0,1)$ mapped to $(2,1)$. Multiplying gives

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta+2\sin\theta&2\cos\theta-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Solving $M\binom xy=\binom xy$ for a non-zero point leads to

$$
\sin\theta+\cos\theta=1.
$$

Within the stated interval the required non-identity case is

$$
\boxed{\theta=\frac\pi2}.
$$

</details>

::: {.question-card #matrices-2025-mj-13}
### 2025 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 1 · 11 marks

A one-way stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $14$ is followed by a rotation anticlockwise about the origin through $\pi/3$. Let the combined matrix be $M$.

**(a)** Show that

$$
2M=\begin{pmatrix}14&-\sqrt3\\14\sqrt3&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**[4]**

**(b)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $M$. **[5]**

**(c)** Find $M^{-1}$. **[2]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}14&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}7&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]7\sqrt3&\frac12\end{pmatrix},
$$

which proves the given result. The condition $Y=mX$ gives

$$
\sqrt3m^2-13m+14\sqrt3=0,
$$

so

$$
\boxed{y=2\sqrt3x\quad\text{or}\quad y=\frac7{\sqrt3}x}.
$$

Finally,

$$
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1/14&\sqrt3/14\\-\sqrt3&1\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

</details>

### 2025 May/June · 9231/14 · Question 5 · 14 marks

A one-way stretch in the $x$-direction with scale factor $3$ is followed by reflection in $y=x$.

**(a)** Find the combined matrix $M$. **[3]**

**(b)** Give full details of the transformation represented by $M^{-1}$. **[3]**

Let $N$ satisfy $MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}$.

**(c)** Find $N$. **[3]**

**(d)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $MN$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$$
\boxed{M=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\3&0\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

$M^{-1}$ represents reflection in $y=x$ followed by a one-way stretch in the $x$-direction with scale factor $1/3$. Also

$$
\boxed{N=M^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&2/3\\1&2\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

For $MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}$, $Y=mX$ gives $2m^2-m-3=0$. Therefore

$$
\boxed{y=\frac32x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
$$

</details>

### 2025 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 2 · 11 marks

Let

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&\frac32\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\frac32&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Describe the transformation represented by $A$. **[2]**

**(b)** Describe the transformation represented by $B$. **[2]**

Triangle $DEF$ is transformed by $AB$ onto triangle $PQR$.

**(c)** Show that the two triangles have the same area. **[2]**

**(d)** Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by $AB$. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

$A$ is a shear with the $x$-axis fixed and $(0,1)$ mapped to $(3/2,1)$. $B$ is a shear with the $y$-axis fixed and $(1,0)$ mapped to $(1,3/2)$. Now

$$
AB=\begin{pmatrix}13/4&3/2\\3/2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \det(AB)=1,
$$

so areas are unchanged. For $y=mx$, $Y=mX$ gives $m^2+\frac32m-1=0$, hence

$$
\boxed{y=-2x\quad\text{or}\quad y=\frac12x}.
$$

</details>

::: {.question-card #matrices-2025-on-12}
### 2025 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 10 marks

Let $k,m$ be non-zero constants and

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&m\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(a)** Describe the transformation represented by $B$ when **(i)** $m=1$, and **(ii)** $m=k$. **[4]**

**(b)** Show that $ABC$ is singular. **[6]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

When $m=1$, $B$ is a one-way stretch parallel to the $x$-axis with scale factor $k$. When $m=k$, $B=kI$ is an enlargement centred at the origin with scale factor $k$.

Multiplication gives

$$
ABC=\begin{pmatrix}
m&m&2m\\
-2k+m&k+m&-k+2m\\
2k+m&-k+m&k+2m
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Expanding its determinant and collecting terms gives

$$
m(k+m)(k+2m)-m(-k+m)(-k+2m)-m(-2k+m)(k+2m)
$$

$$
{}+m(2k+m)(-k+2m)+2m(-2k+m)(-k+m)-2m(2k+m)(k+m)=0.
$$

Hence $\det(ABC)=0$ and $ABC$ is singular.

</details>

:::

::: {.question-card #matrices-2025-on-14}
### 2025 October/November · 9231/14 · Question 5 · 14 marks

**(a)** Show that

$$
\cos\frac\pi{12}=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4},\qquad
\sin\frac\pi{12}=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}.
$$

**[2]**

Let

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&\sin(\pi/12)\\\sin(\pi/12)&-\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}.
$$

**(b)** Give full details of the two transformations represented by $M$, in the correct order. **[4]**

**(c)** Write $M^{-1}$ as the product of two matrices, neither equal to $I$. **[2]**

**(d)** Given that $y=mx$ is invariant, show that

$$
m^2\sin\frac\pi{12}+2m\cos\frac\pi{12}-\sin\frac\pi{12}=0,
$$

and find $m$ in the requested cotangent/cosecant form. **[6]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show answer and mark scheme</summary>

Use the angle difference $\pi/12=\pi/4-\pi/6$ to prove the exact values. The matrix factorises as

$$
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&-\sin(\pi/12)\\\sin(\pi/12)&\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Thus reflect first in the $x$-axis, then rotate anticlockwise through $\pi/12$ about the origin. Reversing the order gives

$$
\boxed{M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&\sin(\pi/12)\\-\sin(\pi/12)&\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}}.
$$

Applying $Y=mX$ produces the stated quadratic. The quadratic formula and $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$ give

$$
\boxed{m=-\cot\frac\pi{12}\pm\cosec\frac\pi{12}}.
$$

</details>
